verdict.summary: Use OAuth so each customer signs in to their own Calendly account. Setup usually takes 3–6 hours. Calendly does not document an app-review wait. For Production, each app has exactly one HTTPS callback URL. Use separate apps for separate callback hosts.
verdict.activeEffort: 3–6 hours, mostly building secure OAuth callbacks and token storage (estimate)
verdict.mainGate: A Production app must have exactly one HTTPS callback URL when real users connect.

recommendation.text: Use a conventional Calendly OAuth app. Create a Sandbox app first. Create a separate Production app for real customer data. Use Calendly MCP only if your product is already an MCP client.

sources.quote: We recommend that you start with a Sandbox app for development. Create a second app for Production when you are ready to use real customer data.
Calendly MCP uses DCR (RFC 7591), so clients self-register to obtain a client_id at runtime.

essentials.text: Access tokens expire after 2 hours. Keep refresh tokens only on your server. Refresh tokens are single-use, so save the replacement token in the same database transaction.

essentials.text: Use PKCE, a proof key that protects the authorization code, with S256. Validate a one-time state value yourself. Verify webhook signatures using the raw body, timestamp, and HMAC-SHA256.

sources.quote: Every OAuth app must use PKCE conforming to RFC 7636, with the `S256` method. If the request does not include a `code_challenge`, it fails.
The signed payload concatenates the timestamp, a period, and the request body.
you can use to reject the webhook if the timestamp in the signature header is too old

requests.text: Generate and retain CODE_VERIFIER, then send the user to this PKCE authorization URL.

sources.quote: Every OAuth app must use Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) with the S256 method. If the authorization request does not include a code challenge, the request fails.

https://auth.calendly.com/oauth/authorize?client_id=CLIENT_ID
& response_type= code
& redirect_uri= REDIRECT_URI
& code_challenge_method= S256
& code_challenge= CODE_CHALLENGE

requests.label: Send the user to sign in

requests.text: Use the same redirect URI and the original PKCE verifier when exchanging the authorization code.

sources.quote: Send a POST request to Get Access Token at https://auth.calendly.com/oauth/token . Include these parameters:

grant_type : authorization_code
code : the authorization code
redirect_uri : the same redirect URI that you used to get the code
client_id : your client ID
code_verifier : the verifier that you generated in step 1
If your app runs on a server, also send your client secret. Use HTTP Basic authentication with your client ID as the username and your client secret as the password.

requests.label: Exchange the code for tokens

detail.text: Connect a test Calendly account through Sandbox. Test token refresh, reconnect after refresh failure, and per-user data separation. Confirm each booking action requires explicit user confirmation.
